brief: Wells Fargo's November outlook leaves full-year GDP growth at 2.4% for 2026 and 2.5% for 2027, essentially unchanged from October, arguing midterm election results and AI-regulation risk do not materially change the growth path. The AI buildout stays intact but set to slow as power and compute constraints bite, even as data-center-driven structures investment accelerated in the third quarter. Labor demand has firmed, with payrolls expected to average 65K per month in 2027 and unemployment holding at 4.1%, consistent with full employment. October's core CPI came in 8bps hot, lifting the core PCE deflator forecast to 3.3% y/y for Q4-2026 before easing toward 2.6% in 2027, which resets the FOMC's hawkish clock: Wells Fargo's baseline is a 25bp December hike with risk of 1-2 more in 2027, and it raised its year-end-2027 10-year Treasury yield forecast to 4.85%. On fiscal policy, the December 11 funding deadline is expected to be punted via another continuing resolution, with the debt ceiling binding around early March and the exhaustion date near early Q4 2027. Globally, the tightening cycle is extending into 2027 across the ECB, BOE, BOC and BOJ, while India's hike was brought forward to December 2026 and Brazil, Mexico and China diverge toward easier policy or stronger growth.
